resolutions.researcher_notes: Replaces the dead attaqa.net original. Value 'construction' supported: PressTV (18 Apr 2023) quotes the Iran Gas Engineering & Development Co. CEO that Iran 'had begun laying the pipeline... from Minab to Kuh Mubarak'; Pipeline Technology Journal (6 Apr 2023) states the first 120-km section Minab-Sirik is 'almost 87% complete' and the second section Sirik-Kuhmobarak 'began in February'. Two separate outlets, though both trace to the same April-2023 NIGC (Reza Noshadi) statement. NOTE/flag: active construction is on the ONSHORE Iranian trunk (Minab-Sirik-Kuhmobarak) toward the coast; the offshore undersea leg to Oman itself is not yet under construction. GEM 'construction' is defensible but reflects the domestic segment.

ProposalYear 2003 supported by Iran International (22 May 2022): 'Iran and Oman signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in 2003 to construct a 200-km pipeline from Iran's Kuh-e Mobarak to Oman's Sohar port'. Single strong source (medium). CONTRADICTION to flag: Anadolu Agency (aa.com.tr) states the two countries 'first signed a Memorandum of Understanding in 2013' - a common alternate origin date some sources use (2013 = the $60bn 25-year supply deal). The 2003 date refers to the earlier MoU; kept as-is per iranintl. Could not verify a clean second independent source stating 2003 explicitly.

Replaces the dead Tehran Times 428285 original. SegmentCost 1,200,000,000 USD supported by two independent outlets: Iran International (2003 MoU 'estimated at the time to cost about $1.2 billion') and Egypt Oil & Gas ('the pipeline project, which is estimated to cost around $1.2 billion'). Both state ~$1.2 billion; value confirmed.

Owner1 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' 100% supported by Egypt Oil & Gas: 'The ministry of petroleum is responsible for carrying out this project that has to be implemented through two undersea and land phases' (quoting NIGC CEO / Deputy Petroleum Minister Hamidreza Araqi). Single strong source (medium). Consistency note: offshore-technology.com profile attributes ownership to 'National Iranian Oil and others' with operation by NIGEC/NIGC - NIGC/NIOC are state entities under the Ministry of Petroleum, so the Ministry-level 100% attribution is consistent, not conflicting.
